camps.name: Cascade-Johannesburg Col bivy
camps.why: Sleeping at the col puts the East Ridge start steps away and splits the couloir from the long ridge day. Tent room is tiny, so bring a bivy sack and expect a cold, exposed night.

camps.name: Johannesburg Camp
camps.why: A walk-in site just above the road end, used the night before to be at the couloir at dawn. It adds a night and does not shorten the summit day, so most parties skip it.

camps.name: Buttress bivy at the heather-to-rock transition
camps.why: The planned stop at the base of the summit glacier, usually reached after 8-12 hours of climbing. It leaves 2-3 hours to the top and has meltwater in summer, though some parties run short.

camps.name: Chopped platforms on the upper glacier
camps.why: A fallback for parties caught by dark above the main bivy: cut a platform in cupped snow and anchor well. Exposed to wind and crevasses, so not a plan, and the summit is no nearer.

new_camps.name: Bivy ledge below the glacier
new_camps.why: The standard night on this rib, at the base of the snow arete. Parties arrive mid-afternoon, leaving only the arete and summit for day two, and the ledge looks straight down on the parking lot.
new_camps.water: Snow was melted at the site on a July trip.
new_camps.permit: A free backcountry permit is needed to camp here.
new_camps.notes: Reached by a steep day of heather, slab and rock from the Cascade Pass trailhead. Parties summit the next morning and return by the East Ridge and Doug's Direct.

camps.name: Johannesburg Camp
camps.why: The only camp on file, a walk-in site near the trailhead. It gives a dawn start at the base but no higher bivy for this line; where parties sleep on the ridge itself is not documented.

plan_conflict: The plan gives no day detail and a 1963-line party has been reported doing it in about 16 hours round trip; a real overnight spot on the ridge was not found, so the trailhead camp stays as the only option.

camps.name: Mesahchie basin, below the col
camps.why: The standard camp for the Ragged Ridge peaks, about five hours from the car. Snow fills the basin early in summer, so flat ground is scarce, but it puts the summit gullies one morning away.

camps.name: Easy Pass trailhead, SR 20
camps.why: The start and finish of the trip, not a camp. Sleeping here means the full 3,000 ft climb to Easy Pass on day one, which adds a long, hot start before any off-trail travel.

camps.name: Ragged Ridge crest bivy, south of Mesahchie Col
camps.why: A higher, more committing bivy on the crest near 7,000 ft. It saves the approach descent and shortens the summit day, but offers little shelter and water must be carried or melted.

camps.name: Fisher Camp, Fisher Creek basin
camps.why: A forested, sheltered camp below Easy Pass on the far side, with permits limited. It is a longer way round to the peaks, so parties choose it for comfort and the Fisher Creek approach to Kimtah.

camps.name: Eldorado-Inspiration snow arm high camp
camps.why: A snow camp near 7,500 ft that cuts the following day's glacier distance to the col. Water comes from melting snow, and the exact ground shifts with the snowpack.

camps.name: Klawatti Col camp
camps.why: Sits right under the North Ridge, so the summit is about one to two hours away. Reached by roped travel across the Inspiration Glacier; rock islands give flat tent spots.

camps.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
camps.why: A road campground to sleep at the night before when the permit must be picked up in person. It adds no mileage and only makes the first morning easier.

camps.name: Eldorado East Ridge rock bivies
camps.why: Bare rock at the East Ridge base gives a firmer, drier platform than snow when the snow has melted back. Sits near the same height as the snow arm, so it is a swap, not a gain.

camps.name: Eldorado Basin camp
camps.why: A lower, vegetated camp with running water and warmer nights, good for a late start. It leaves about 1,500 ft more climbing to the glacier on day two.

camps.name: Roush Creek Basin camp
camps.why: A neighbouring basin to use if Eldorado Basin is full, with room between 6,100 and 6,400 ft. The extra traverse back toward the glacier makes day two longer.

plan_conflict: The plan's day two reads as summit-then-return, but parties usually carry to Klawatti Col on day two and climb from there; Marble Creek is marked main on file but is only a night-before option.

camps.name: Eldorado Basin camp
camps.why: Treeline camp with running water and the normal first night on the four-day plan, after the boulder field and cliff band. Gives a short second day onto the glacier.

camps.name: Klawatti Col camp
camps.why: The high camp for this side: rock islands beside the glacier put Klawatti within a day's reach. Parties melt snow for water and return here after the summit.

camps.name: Eldorado-Inspiration snow arm high camp
camps.why: A snow camp on the way up that parties use instead of pressing on to the col. It is a shorter day two but adds distance to the Klawatti Glacier.

camps.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
camps.why: A road campground for the night before when the permit must be activated in person. It is not slept at during the trip itself.

camps.name: Eldorado East Ridge rock bivies
camps.why: Flat rock at the base of the East Ridge when the snow has melted back, firmer than the glacier. A swap for the snow arm camp, not an extra night.

camps.name: Roush Creek Basin camp
camps.why: A neighbouring basin with space for a night one camp when Eldorado Basin is busy, roughly 6,100-6,400 ft. It adds a traverse toward the col on day two.

plan_conflict: On file Eldorado Basin camp is a route option and the snow arm and Marble Creek camps are marked main, but the plan sleeps at Eldorado Basin night 1 and Klawatti Col nights 2-3, so roles were changed.

camps.name: Pelton Basin
camps.why: Established camp below Cascade Pass; the east-end bench of the basin puts you an easy walk from the Yawning Glacier. No camping on the pass itself, and summer weekends fill up.

camps.name: Pelton Basin
camps.why: Established camp below Cascade Pass, a short walk from the Yawning Glacier and the couloir base. Camping at the pass itself is not allowed, and summer weekends can be busy.

new_camps.name: Kool-Aid Lake
new_camps.why: The standard overnight south of Cache Col, about 700 ft below the pass. It puts the ridge within a short walk and leaves the exit over Cache Col for the next day.
new_camps.water: A small tarn, which has run dry in some seasons.
new_camps.notes: Reached by a boot path from Cache Col, over snow in early season. A small, well-used site, so expect to share it.

camps.name: Kool-Aid Lake
camps.why: The usual first camp south of Cache Col, about 700 ft below the pass. Sits at the foot of Magic's south side, with a short summit day; the tarn can run low late in summer.

plan_conflict: One two-day party instead bivied on the 8,200 ft col between Katsuk and Mesahchie, higher than the basin camp on file.

camps.name: Johannesburg Camp
camps.why: A walk-in site just above the trailhead. It is the night-before option, but it adds a night and leaves the whole Cache Glacier approach for summit morning.

new_camps.name: Cache Col camp
new_camps.why: The high camp for the Cache Glacier side: a short glacier walk to Gunsight Notch. Room is limited and there is no stream, so carry water or melt snow.
new_camps.water: Snow only; the nearest lake is Kool-Aid Lake below the col.
new_camps.capacity: Room for two tents just east of the col and one spot just west.
new_camps.permit: Outside the national park, so no permit is needed.
new_camps.notes: Sits on the shoulder above the col, a spot parties often stay for several nights. Wind can be strong.

plan_conflict: Johannesburg Camp is marked main on file but sits near the trailhead; the plan's night 1 is a camp near Cache Col, so it was changed to a route option.

camps.name: Head of Kindy Creek and the Kindy-Buck Creek pass
camps.why: The camps that put Buckindy in range: basins near the head of Kindy Creek or the pass beside it. Sleeping here makes the glacier summit day a round trip from the tent.

camps.name: Horse Lake saddle camp
camps.why: The first night's camp on the Green Mountain approach, with slow sidehill travel ahead. It is a stop on the long walk in, not a base for the summit day.

plan_conflict: The plan says the approach alone takes two or three days, so the real trip is longer than three days and a night at Horse Lake saddle or similar comes before the Kindy Creek camps.

camps.name: Jug Lake
camps.why: The most-used base on this side, but the plan's real camp is a heather bench near 6,100 ft above it. Jug Lake is lower and brushy, so the summit day from here is much longer.

plan_conflict: The plan puts night 1 at a heather bench near 6,100 ft below the west face, not at Jug Lake (3,911 ft); only camping near 6,000 ft was found for the west side, with no named site or measured elevation.
